name: Cylinder Cover for Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Cylinder Cover
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 550XP Mark II cylinder cover. Protects the top end, guides cooling air and gives access to the plug and air filter on this 50cc saw.
tagline: Replacement top cover for the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II, for cracked or lost covers.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP Mark II cylinder cover replaces the top cover that sits over the engine, spark plug and air filter. A cracked or missing cover lets chips into the intake area and upsets cooling airflow, so it is worth replacing rather than taping up.
highlights: Replacement top cover for the 550XP Mark II
Shields the air filter, plug and cylinder from chips
Helps direct cooling air over the cylinder fins
Good fix for covers cracked in a fall or lost on the job
Order by model; covers differ between the original 550XP and the Mark II

p: The cylinder cover is the big top shroud on the 550XP Mark II. It keeps sawdust, rain and debris off the air filter and spark plug, and it forms part of the path the flywheel pushes cooling air through. A saw that runs without it, or with a cover that is split open, pulls more dirt toward the intake and can run hotter than it should.

On a 50cc saw that gets used for limbing, bucking brush and storm cleanup, covers take a beating. Drops off the tailgate, a log rolling onto the saw or a cold morning crack around a latch are the usual causes.

A cover that does not seal well also lets fine dust reach the air filter faster, so the filter clogs sooner and the saw loses power through the day. If you have been cleaning the filter more often than usual, a loose or cracked cover may be the reason. Fitting a new one is quick, costs little next to engine wear, and keeps the saw looking and running like a working tool should.

Swapping the cover is a hand-tool job: release the cover fasteners, lift the old cover off and seat the new one so it sits flat with no gaps around the edges. Check the air filter and plug while you have it off, and clean out packed chips around the cylinder fins.
The original 550XP and the Mark II are different saws, so match the part to your model before you order. For more service parts, browse our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Will this cover fit the original 550XP?
faq.a: Do not assume it will. The Mark II has its own parts, so check the part listing or your dealer's parts lookup against your exact model before ordering.

faq.q: Can I run the saw with a cracked cover?
faq.a: A small crack is not an emergency, but a cover that lets chips into the air filter area or rattles loose should be replaced soon to protect the engine.

name: Cylinder Gasket for Husqvarna 390XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 390XP Cylinder Gasket
meta: Husqvarna 390XP cylinder gasket for top-end rebuilds on this 88cc saw. Why a fresh base gasket matters, when to replace it and what to check during the job.
tagline: Base gasket for the Husqvarna 390XP cylinder, for top-end rebuilds and repairs.
summary: This Husqvarna 390XP cylinder gasket seals the joint between the cylinder and crankcase on the big 88cc saw. Any time the cylinder comes off for a piston, ring or cylinder job, a new gasket goes back on.
highlights: Cylinder base gasket for the Husqvarna 390XP
Seals the cylinder to the crankcase
Replace every time the cylinder is removed
Cheap insurance against air leaks after a rebuild
Keep one on hand when you order top-end parts

body.h: Why a new gasket every time
p: A two-stroke engine depends on a sealed crankcase. If air sneaks in at the cylinder base, the mix goes lean, the saw races or hangs at high idle, and the engine runs hot. On a big-bore saw like the 390XP that is pulling long bars through hardwood, a lean condition can scuff a piston fast.
Gaskets crush and take a set when they are torqued down. Reusing one is a gamble, and the gasket costs a fraction of what the rest of the job does.

The 390XP is often the saw that comes out for big removals, large stump work and milling, so it tends to run hard for long stretches. That makes a good seal more important, not less. If the saw was scored from a lean condition in the first place, find the source of the leak before reassembly, whether it is a cracked intake boot, a tired crank seal or a clogged fuel filter. A gasket alone will not fix those.

Clean both mating surfaces carefully without gouging them, fit the new gasket dry unless the service manual says otherwise, and torque the cylinder fasteners evenly in a cross pattern to spec. A pressure and vacuum test after reassembly is the best way to confirm the engine is sealed.
If you are not set up for engine work, a Husqvarna dealer can do the job. More service parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Do I need a new cylinder gasket if I only replace the piston rings?
faq.a: Yes. Removing the cylinder disturbs the old gasket, so fit a new one whenever the cylinder comes off.

faq.q: Should I use sealant with this gasket?
faq.a: Follow the Husqvarna service manual for your saw. Adding sealant where it is not called for can push material into the engine or affect port timing.

name: Cylinder Gasket for Husqvarna 572XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 572XP Cylinder Gasket
meta: Husqvarna 572XP cylinder gasket for top-end work on this 70cc pro saw. Seals the cylinder base to the crankcase. Replace it any time the cylinder comes off.
tagline: Cylinder base gasket for the Husqvarna 572XP, needed for any top-end job.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP cylinder gasket seals the base of the cylinder to the crankcase. It is a must-have part for piston, ring or cylinder replacement on the 572XP.
highlights: Cylinder base gasket for the Husqvarna 572XP
Keeps the crankcase sealed against air leaks
Single-use part: replace whenever the cylinder is pulled
Pairs with a cylinder assembly or piston kit
Inexpensive part to order with any top-end job

body.h: Where it fits in a rebuild
p: The 572XP is a workhorse felling and bucking saw, and it is worth keeping alive with proper parts. When the top end comes apart, whether for a scored piston, worn rings or a new cylinder, the base gasket is one of the parts you should not reuse.

An air leak at the base leans out the engine. Symptoms include a hanging idle, a saw that will not settle back down after you let off the throttle, and extra heat. Left alone, that can undo all the work of the rebuild.

It is worth ordering the gasket at the same time as the cylinder or piston, not after the saw is in pieces on the bench. A saw waiting on a seven-dollar part is a saw that is not working. Some mechanics keep a few base gaskets for each crew saw on the shelf for exactly that reason. Store them flat and dry so they do not crease or pick up oil before use.

Clean the crankcase and cylinder mating surfaces, fit the new gasket in the correct orientation, and torque the cylinder fasteners evenly to the figure in the service manual. Pressure and vacuum test the engine before it goes back to work.
Also replace anything else that looks tired while the saw is apart, such as the intake boot or fuel line. Find matching items in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Is the 572XP gasket the same as the 372XP gasket?
faq.a: They are different saws with different engines. Order the gasket listed for the 572XP.

faq.q: What causes a cylinder base air leak?
faq.a: Reused or damaged gaskets, dirty or damaged mating surfaces and uneven bolt torque are the usual causes.

name: Decompression Valve for Husqvarna 372XP X-Torque
title: Husqvarna 372XP Decompression Valve (X-Torque)
meta: Husqvarna 372XP decompression valve for the X-Torque saw. Makes the 70cc engine easier to pull over. Signs of a leaking valve and how to replace it safely.
tagline: Replacement decompression valve that makes the 372XP X-Torque easier to start.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP decompression valve bleeds off compression while you pull the starter, so the 70cc X-Torque saw is easier to start. A worn or stuck valve can leak compression while the saw is running or make starting a fight.
highlights: Replacement decompression valve for the 372XP X-Torque
Reduces compression for easier starting
Fix for a valve that leaks, sticks or is damaged
Threads into the cylinder
Clean carbon off the valve area during service

p: You push the decompression button before pulling the cord. That opens a small passage in the cylinder so the piston is not fighting full compression on the starting pull. Once the engine fires, combustion pressure closes the valve and it stays shut while you work.

Over time carbon builds up on the valve seat, or the valve gets knocked in a fall. A valve that does not seal causes hard starting, low compression readings and a weak saw. One that sticks shut makes the saw harder to pull.

Climbers and ground crew who start saws many times a day notice a bad valve quickly. If the 372XP suddenly takes more effort to pull or kicks back on the cord, check the valve before blaming the starter. Carbon on the valve tip is often the first problem, and it can come from a rich mix, poor oil or a lot of idling. Cleaning the valve sometimes helps, but a worn valve should be replaced.

With the saw cool and the top cover off, unscrew the old valve from the cylinder, clean the threads and seat area, and install the new valve to the torque in the service manual. Do not overtighten it into an aluminum cylinder.
If a compression test still reads low after a new valve, the problem is likely rings or the cylinder itself. Browse related chainsaw parts for top-end components.

faq.q: How do I know the decompression valve is bad?
faq.a: Common signs are low compression, a hiss from the valve with the engine turning over, or a button that stays down or will not stay pushed in.

faq.q: Does it fit the older non-X-Torque 372XP?
faq.a: Check the parts listing for your exact model and serial range before ordering.

name: Front Handle Assembly for Husqvarna 572XP
title: Husqvarna 572XP Front Handle Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 572XP front handle assembly to replace a bent or cracked handlebar. Restores a solid, safe grip on this pro saw, plus what to check when fitting it.
tagline: Replacement front handlebar assembly for a bent or damaged Husqvarna 572XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP front handle assembly replaces the wraparound front handlebar on the 570-class pro saw. A bent or cracked handle changes how the saw sits in your hands and how well you can control kickback, so it should be replaced, not straightened.
highlights: Front handle assembly for the Husqvarna 572XP
Restores a solid grip for control in the cut
Replace bent, cracked or loose handlebars
Mounts through the anti-vibration system
Check the AV elements while the handle is off

p: The front handle is your main point of control when the bar kicks, pinches or climbs out of a cut. A handle that has been bent from a dropped saw or a log rolling over it can put your left hand in the wrong place and reduce your leverage at the worst moment.
Bending an aluminum or tubular handle back into shape weakens it. A new assembly is the safe repair, and it is a common fix on saws that see hard felling and bucking work.

Check the handle after any hard drop, a saw that got pinned under a log or a tree that sat back on the bar. Look for kinks, cracks near the mounts and play between the handle and the saw body. A handle that is slightly out of line can be hard to spot by eye, so compare the gap at the hand guard with a known good saw if you run more than one 572XP.

The handle attaches to the saw body and connects through anti-vibration elements. Remove the old handle, inspect the AV springs or rubber mounts and replace any that are torn or stretched, then fit the new handle and tighten the fasteners to spec.
Before going back to work, confirm the chain brake hand guard moves freely and engages properly. Matching AV elements are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Can I straighten a bent front handle?
faq.a: It is not recommended. Bending weakens the handle, and a failure in the cut could cost you control of the saw. Replace it.

faq.q: Do I need special tools?
faq.a: Standard hand tools usually cover it. Follow the Husqvarna service manual for the fastener sequence and torque.

name: Front Handle for Husqvarna T540i XP
title: Husqvarna T540i XP Front Handle Replacement
h1: Husqvarna T540i XP Front Handle Replacement
meta: Husqvarna T540i XP front handle replacement for the battery top-handle saw. Fixes cracked or loose handles on a climbing saw. Fitting notes and safety checks.
tagline: Replacement front handle for the Husqvarna T540i XP battery top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540i XP front handle replaces the front grip on Husqvarna's battery top-handle saw. Climbers lean on that handle for control in the tree, so a cracked or loose handle should be swapped before the saw goes back aloft.
highlights: Replacement front handle for the T540i XP
Restores a firm grip on a climbing saw
Fix for handles cracked from drops or rope strikes
Simple swap with hand tools
Keep the saw's safety features in working order

p: Top-handle saws get dropped onto lanyards, banged against stems and stuffed into saddle holsters all day. The front handle can crack at the mounting points or start to flex. On a battery saw used for pruning and removals in the canopy, a handle that moves is a control problem.
Top-handle chainsaws are built for trained arborists working in trees. Two-handed operation is the standard practice under ANSI Z133, and a sound front handle is part of that.

A sound front handle also matters when you hand the saw down on a tag line or clip it back to your saddle. Grabbing a cracked handle in a hurry is how saws get fumbled out of trees. Look at the mounting points each time you clean the saw, and replace the handle at the first sign of cracks, flex or stripped screw bosses rather than waiting for it to fail aloft.

Remove the battery first. Then remove the fasteners that hold the old handle, fit the new handle in the same orientation and tighten the screws to spec without stripping the plastic. Check that nothing interferes with the chain brake hand guard.
Look over the rest of the saw while it is on the bench. Other T540i XP pieces, from the hand guard to the air filter cover, are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Will this fit the gas T540XP?
faq.a: No. The T540i XP is a battery saw with its own housing parts. Order the handle listed for the gas T540XP if that is your saw.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the battery to change the handle?
faq.a: Yes. Always remove the battery before any service work on a battery chainsaw.

name: Fuel Filter for Husqvarna 3120XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 3120XP Fuel Filter Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 3120XP fuel filter for the 118.8cc big-timber saw. Why a clean in-tank filter matters, signs of a clog and how to swap it in minutes.
tagline: In-tank fuel filter for the Husqvarna 3120XP big-bore chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 3120XP fuel filter is the in-tank pickup filter for the largest saw in the Husqvarna lineup. A 118.8cc engine pulling a long bar burns a lot of fuel, and a partially clogged filter will starve it under load.
highlights: In-tank fuel filter for the Husqvarna 3120XP
Keeps debris out of the carburetor
Fixes bogging and power loss from fuel starvation
Quick swap with a hooked wire
Change with the air filter and plug at tune-up time

p: A big saw that starts and idles fine, then falls on its face when you bury the bar in a large trunk, is often short on fuel. The filter is the first and cheapest thing to check. Running lean under load is hard on any two-stroke, and on a saw this size the repair bill adds up fast.
Debris gets in from dirty fuel cans and from chips around the cap when you refuel on the stump.

Crews running a 3120XP usually save it for the largest trunks, stump flushing and big hardwood. That means the saw may sit for weeks between jobs, and stale fuel left in the tank leaves varnish that can coat the filter. Drain the tank before storage or run pre-mixed fuel, and swap the filter at the start of the season so the saw is ready when the big wood shows up.

Drain the tank, then fish the fuel line out with a hooked wire, taking care not to stretch or tear the line. Pull the old filter off, push the new one on firmly and let it drop back to the bottom of the tank. Inspect the fuel line while it is out and replace it if it is hard or cracked.
Clean the area around the cap before opening it and mix fresh fuel in a clean can. More tune-up items are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How often should I replace the 3120XP fuel filter?
faq.a: Follow the operator manual, and at minimum change it once a season. Replace it sooner if the saw starts bogging under load.

faq.q: Can a clogged fuel filter damage the engine?
faq.a: It can. Fuel starvation makes the engine run lean and hot, which can score the piston and cylinder.

name: Fuel Filter for Husqvarna 545, 550XP and 562XP
title: Husqvarna 550XP Fuel Filter (545, 562XP)
meta: Husqvarna 550XP fuel filter that also fits the 545 and 562XP. Keeps fuel clean for the carburetor. Signs of a clogged filter and how to replace it quickly.
tagline: In-tank fuel filter for Husqvarna 545, 550XP and 562XP chainsaws.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP fuel filter is listed to fit the 545, 550XP and 562XP, which makes it a handy spare for crews running more than one of these saws. It sits on the end of the fuel line in the tank and keeps grit out of the carburetor.
highlights: In-tank fuel filter for the 545, 550XP and 562XP
One spare part covers several common crew saws
Fixes bogging caused by fuel starvation
Easy to change in the field
Pair with a new plug and clean air filter

p: The 545, 550XP and 562XP are common ground saws on tree crews, used for limbing, bucking and feeding the chipper. Fuel filters wear out quietly, and the first sign is usually a saw that will not hold full throttle. Having one filter that fits several saws keeps the parts bin simple.
If you run Mark II versions, confirm fitment for your model before ordering.

A clogged filter often gets mistaken for a carburetor problem. Before adjusting the mix screws or ordering a carb kit, pull the filter and look at it. If it is dark, gummy or packed with debris, replace it and test the saw again. Many times that is all it takes. Keep a few in the truck, since a ten-dollar part should never be the reason a saw sits out a day.

Drain the tank, hook the fuel line out through the filler neck and pull the old filter off. Push the new one on firmly so it cannot slip off, then drop it back to the bottom of the tank. Replace the fuel line too if it is stiff, cracked or swollen.
Keep the saw's fuel fresh and the cap area clean, and the filter will last longer. More service items are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Does this filter fit the 550XP Mark II?
faq.a: Check the parts listing for your model. Fitment can change between versions, so confirm before ordering.

faq.q: What are the signs of a bad chainsaw fuel filter?
faq.a: Bogging or dying under throttle, loss of power in the cut and a saw that will not keep running after starting.

name: Fuel Line for Husqvarna 562XP
title: Husqvarna 562XP Fuel Line Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 562XP fuel line. Fix leaks, air in the fuel system and lean running from hard or cracked lines. When to replace it and fitting tips.
tagline: Replacement fuel line for the Husqvarna 562XP chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 562XP fuel line carries fuel from the tank to the carburetor on the 60cc pro saw. Fuel lines harden and crack with age and ethanol fuel, and a leaking line can cause hard starting, lean running and a fuel smell around the saw.
highlights: Replacement fuel line for the Husqvarna 562XP
Fixes leaks and air entering the fuel system
Swap it when it turns hard, cracked or swollen
Fit a new fuel filter at the same time
Restores steady fuel delivery to the carburetor

body.h: Signs of a failing fuel line
p: A cracked fuel line lets air into the system. The saw may start and die, run rough or rev erratically, or leak fuel where the line passes through the tank. Old lines also go hard and can break when you fish the filter out.
Ethanol-blended fuel tends to shorten fuel line life. Saws that sit between jobs with fuel in the tank are the most likely to need a new line.

A quick way to spot a bad line is to look at where it passes through the tank wall. Fuel weeping there, a wet spot under the saw after it sits, or a line that feels stiff when you fish the filter out are all signs. Ethanol-free or pre-mixed fuel helps lines last longer, and draining the tank before long storage keeps the rubber from drying out between seasons.

Fuel line replacement on the 562XP means getting at the carburetor connection and feeding the new line through the tank grommet so it seals. Take your time and do not cut or nick the new line. Fit a new fuel filter on the tank end while you are there.
If you are not comfortable working around the carburetor, a dealer can do it quickly. Find a matching filter in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Can I use universal fuel line on a 562XP?
faq.a: The OEM line is shaped and sized to seal in the tank and fit the carburetor. Using the part listed for your saw avoids leaks and fit problems.

faq.q: Should I replace the fuel filter too?
faq.a: Yes. It is inexpensive and you already have the line out.

name: Fuel and Oil Cap Assembly for Husqvarna T540XP Mark II
keyword: husqvarna t540xp mark ii fuel cap
title: Husqvarna T540XP Mark II Fuel Cap and Oil Cap
h1: Husqvarna T540XP Mark II Fuel Cap and Oil Cap
meta: Husqvarna T540XP Mark II fuel cap and oil cap assembly. Replaces leaking, cracked or lost caps on this top-handle climbing saw. Fitting and care tips inside.
tagline: Replacement fuel or bar oil tank cap for the Husqvarna T540XP Mark II top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540XP Mark II fuel cap assembly replaces a leaking, cracked or lost tank cap on the gas top-handle saw. A cap that does not seal can drip fuel or bar oil on your saddle and clothing, or let debris into the tank.
highlights: Replacement tank cap assembly for the T540XP Mark II
Stops leaks from worn seals or cracked caps
Keeps sawdust and water out of the tanks
Fix for caps lost in the tree or on the job
Check the cap seal at every refuel

body.h: Why a good cap matters on a climbing saw
p: A top-handle saw hangs off your saddle at odd angles all day. A cap with a worn seal will weep fuel or oil onto your gear and down your leg. That is a mess, a fire risk around a hot muffler and a slip hazard on the saw's handle.
Caps also get cross-threaded, cracked or dropped from the canopy. Carrying a spare is cheap insurance on a long removal.

Mark the caps with a paint pen if your crew has trouble telling fuel and oil apart on the ground, especially if several saws share a fueling station. Mixing them up is a costly mistake. Some climbers also clip a spare cap in the saw kit, since it is easy to set a cap on a limb during refueling aloft and watch it roll off into the brush below.

Confirm which tank your cap is for, since fuel and bar oil caps are often marked differently. Clean the filler neck threads before fitting the new cap and tighten it by hand until it seats. Wipe chips away from the cap before opening it to refuel.
If the saw still leaks with a new cap, check the tank vent and the tank itself. More T540XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Does this cap fit the original T540XP?
faq.a: Check the parts listing for your exact model before ordering. Mark II parts are not always interchangeable with earlier versions.

faq.q: Why does my saw leak bar oil when stored?
faq.a: Some oil seepage from the bar oil system is normal on many saws. Store the saw upright and check that the cap seal is in good shape.

name: Husqvarna Fuel Tank and Oil Cap Assembly
title: Husqvarna Chainsaw Fuel Cap and Oil Cap Assembly
h1: Husqvarna Chainsaw Fuel Cap and Oil Cap Assembly
meta: Replacement Husqvarna chainsaw fuel cap and oil cap assembly. Fixes leaks and lost caps. Confirm fitment for your saw model before ordering. Tips inside.
tagline: Replacement fuel or bar oil cap assembly for Husqvarna chainsaws.
summary: This Husqvarna chainsaw fuel cap assembly replaces a worn, cracked or lost tank cap. Caps vary between saw models, so check the parts listing for your exact saw before ordering.
highlights: Replacement tank cap assembly for Husqvarna saws
Stops fuel or oil seeping from a worn seal
Keeps debris and water out of the tank
Spare worth carrying in the saw box
Confirm fitment by model before ordering
specs: Fuel or bar oil tank cap assembly
Check the parts listing for your model

p: Tank caps wear in a few predictable ways. The rubber seal flattens or tears and the cap weeps. The threads or locking tabs crack from being overtightened or dropped. Or the cap simply goes missing on a jobsite. Any of these can let fuel out or let chips and water in, and contaminated fuel leads to clogged filters and carburetor trouble.
A cap that leaks fuel near a hot muffler is a fire risk, so do not put it off.

If your saw has been leaking from the cap for a while, wipe down the area and check for damage to the filler neck too. A cracked neck will leak no matter how good the cap is. Also check that you are using the right cap on the right tank. Mixing up fuel and oil caps on saws that use different parts for each tank is a common cause of leaks.

Husqvarna uses different caps across its saw range, and fuel and oil caps are not always the same part. Check your model and the cap markings before ordering. Clean the filler threads, fit the new cap by hand and make sure it seats fully.
Browse our chainsaw parts section for model-specific caps and other service items.

faq.q: Which Husqvarna saws does this cap fit?
faq.a: Fitment depends on the saw model. Check the parts listing or a Husqvarna parts lookup for your saw before ordering.

faq.q: How tight should a chainsaw fuel cap be?
faq.a: Hand tight until it seats. Using tools or forcing it can crack the cap or damage the seal.

name: Husqvarna 372XP O-Ring for Clutch Side Crankshaft Seal
title: Husqvarna 372XP Crankshaft Seal O-Ring, Clutch Side
h1: Husqvarna 372XP Crankshaft Seal O-Ring, Clutch Side
meta: Husqvarna 372XP crankshaft seal O-ring for the clutch side. A small part that helps keep the crankcase sealed. When to replace it and why air leaks matter.
tagline: O-ring for the clutch side crankshaft seal on the Husqvarna 372XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP crankshaft seal O-ring is used with the clutch side seal to help keep the crankcase sealed. It is a small, inexpensive part to replace whenever the clutch side seal is serviced.
highlights: O-ring for the 372XP clutch side crankshaft seal
Helps keep the crankcase sealed
Replace along with the seal during service
Inexpensive part for an important job
Useful for 372XP rebuilds and leak repairs

p: A two-stroke engine uses crankcase pressure to move the fuel charge. If air leaks in past a crankshaft seal, the engine runs lean. Signs include a high or hanging idle, a saw that will not tune properly and extra heat. On a 372XP that is felling and bucking all day, that can lead to a scored piston.
Seals harden with age and heat, and the clutch side seal also sees heat from the clutch and bar oil.

Small parts like this are easy to forget when ordering for a rebuild, and the saw can end up waiting on a five-dollar O-ring. Make a parts list from the Husqvarna diagram for your saw before you start, and order seals, O-rings and gaskets together. Store spare O-rings in a sealed bag away from fuel and sunlight so the rubber does not dry out or swell before use.

Replacing crankshaft seals is a job for someone comfortable with engine work. The clutch and oil pump drive must come off to reach the seal. Install the new seal and O-ring without nicking them and follow the service manual. A pressure and vacuum test confirms the job.
If you are replacing seals, consider the flywheel side seal as well. More 372XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How do I know the crankshaft seal is leaking?
faq.a: A pressure and vacuum test is the reliable way. Symptoms include a hanging or erratic idle and a saw that runs lean.

faq.q: Can I replace the seal without splitting the case?
faq.a: On many saws the clutch side seal can be replaced with the case together using the right tools. Follow the service manual for your saw.

name: Husqvarna 395XP On/Off Switch
title: Husqvarna 395XP On/Off Switch Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 395XP on/off switch. A saw that will not stop or will not start may have a bad stop switch. Signs, safety notes and fitting tips here.
tagline: Replacement stop switch for the Husqvarna 395XP big-bore chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP on/off switch is the stop switch that grounds the ignition to shut the engine down. A faulty switch can stop the 94cc saw from starting, or worse, stop it from shutting off.
highlights: Replacement stop switch for the Husqvarna 395XP
Restores reliable engine shutoff
Fixes no-start problems caused by a shorted switch
Check the ground wire while you are in there
Important safety part on a big saw

p: On a big saw like the 395XP, being able to kill the engine instantly is a safety requirement. A worn or broken switch, or a damaged wire, can leave the saw running when you hit stop. Do not keep working with a saw that will not shut off.
The opposite failure is common too: a switch or wire that shorts to ground will keep the saw from making a spark, so it will not start at all.

Switches wear out from use, but they also get knocked, packed with sawdust and soaked in bar oil. Keep the area around the switch clean, and check that it clicks firmly between positions. If the switch feels mushy or moves without much resistance, test the saw's stop function before your next job, and plan a replacement. A dependable stop switch is part of running any saw safely.

With the saw off and cool, remove the covers needed to reach the switch and disconnect the wire. Fit the new switch, reconnect the wire and route it so it cannot rub through on a sharp edge. Test that the saw starts and that the switch stops it every time before it goes back in service.
If you are unsure about ignition wiring, have a dealer do it. More 395XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: My saw will not turn off. Is it the switch?
faq.a: Often it is the switch or its wire. Stop using the saw and repair it before it goes back to work. Choke the engine to stall it if needed.

faq.q: Can a bad switch cause no spark?
faq.a: Yes. If the switch or its wire is grounding the ignition all the time, the saw will not make a spark.

name: Husqvarna 572XP Ignition Module Assembly
title: Husqvarna 572XP Ignition Module Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 572XP ignition module assembly for no-spark and weak-spark problems. How to confirm it is the module, fitting tips and setting the air gap right.
tagline: Replacement ignition coil and module for the Husqvarna 572XP chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP ignition module assembly replaces the coil that makes spark for the 70cc pro saw. When a 572XP has fuel and compression but no spark, or quits once it is hot, the ignition module is a common suspect.
highlights: Ignition module assembly for the Husqvarna 572XP
Fix for no spark or weak spark
Can cure saws that die when hot and restart when cool
Set the flywheel air gap correctly on install
Rule out the plug and stop switch first

p: Before buying a module, check the cheap things. Fit a new spark plug, inspect the plug lead and boot, and check the stop switch wire for a short to ground. Then use a spark tester. No spark with a good plug and switch points to the module.
A module that is failing can also act up only when hot. If the saw runs fine, dies after a few tanks and restarts after cooling, the coil is a good suspect.

Ignition modules are not cheap, so it pays to be sure before buying. Swapping in a module from another 572XP, if your shop has one, is the fastest way to confirm a diagnosis. Also check the flywheel for damaged magnets or a sheared key, which can mimic a bad coil. Some 572XP saws use a different listed ignition part, so match your saw's model and serial before ordering.

The module mounts next to the flywheel. Set the gap between the module and the flywheel magnets to the figure in the service manual, using a gauge, and tighten the screws evenly. A gap that is too wide gives weak spark.
Reconnect the stop switch wire and route the plug lead so it is not pinched. For the related 572XP MP part and other ignition items, see our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How do I check the 572XP for spark?
faq.a: Use an inline spark tester or a known good plug grounded to the cylinder, and pull the cord with the switch in the run position.

faq.q: What air gap does the module need?
faq.a: Use the specification in the Husqvarna service manual and a proper gap gauge.

name: Husqvarna 572XP MP Ignition Module Assembly
title: Husqvarna 572XP MP Ignition Module Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 572XP MP ignition module assembly for later 572XP saws. Confirm your saw's version by serial number, then fix no-spark or hot-stall problems.
tagline: Ignition module assembly listed as the MP version for the Husqvarna 572XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP MP ignition module assembly is the MP-listed version of the coil for the 572XP. Husqvarna has used more than one ignition part across 572XP production, so match the part to your saw's model and serial before ordering.
highlights: Ignition module assembly, MP version, for the 572XP
Fix for no-spark or weak-spark conditions
Can cure hot-stall problems from a failing coil
Confirm variant and serial range before ordering
Set the flywheel air gap with a gauge

p: Husqvarna updates parts during a model's run, and the 572XP is no exception. The MP listing is a separate part from the standard 572XP module listed elsewhere on this site. The safest way to order is to look up your saw's model and serial number in a Husqvarna parts lookup or ask a dealer, then match the part number.
If in doubt, do not guess. Ignition parts are generally not returnable once installed.

The model and serial number are on a label on the saw body. Write them down before you order any ignition part, and keep them in your records with the date you bought the saw. That makes it much easier to get the right part quickly the next time the saw needs work. A dealer can also confirm fitment if you give them that number over the phone.
Rule out the spark plug, plug lead and stop switch wiring first, then check spark with a tester. A coil that is dead, weak, or fails only when the saw is hot is a good candidate for replacement.
Mount the new module, set the air gap to the flywheel with a gauge to the service manual figure, and tighten evenly. Find the standard module and other parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: What is the difference between the 572XP and 572XP MP ignition modules?
faq.a: They are listed as separate parts for different 572XP versions. Check your saw's model and serial number against the parts listing to know which one you need.

faq.q: Can a bad ignition module cause hard starting?
faq.a: Yes. Weak spark can make a saw hard to start, especially when warm.

name: Husqvarna 592XP Front Anti-Vibration Element
title: Husqvarna 592XP Anti-Vibration Element, Front Mount
meta: Husqvarna 592XP anti-vibration element for the front mount. Restores a solid handle feel and cuts vibration on this 92.7cc saw. Signs of worn AV mounts.
tagline: Front anti-vibration element for the Husqvarna 592XP big-bore chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 592XP anti-vibration element replaces a front AV mount on the 92.7cc saw. Worn or broken AV elements make the saw feel loose and buzzy in your hands, which adds fatigue and reduces control on long cuts.
highlights: Front anti-vibration element for the Husqvarna 592XP
Restores a firm, controlled handle feel
Reduces vibration reaching your hands and arms
Replace broken, stretched or loose elements
Inspect all AV mounts while the saw is apart

p: The anti-vibration system isolates the engine from the handles. When an element wears out or breaks, the handles start to feel sloppy, the saw droops or twists in your grip, and you feel more buzz through your hands. On a big saw that is running a long bar through large wood, that wears you out fast.
Long exposure to vibration is linked to hand-arm problems, so keeping AV mounts in good shape is a health issue, not just a comfort one.

Big saws like the 592XP spend a lot of time running long bars through big wood, so AV mounts work harder than on a smaller saw. Grab both handles and gently twist the saw with the engine off. A little movement is normal, but a clunk or a lot of free play means a mount is worn or broken. Catching it early keeps the saw comfortable and controllable through a long day.

Access depends on the mount location. Remove the covers or handle parts needed to reach the front element, take the old one out and install the new one, seating it fully. Tighten fasteners to the service manual figure.
If one element has failed, check the others too. More 592XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How many anti-vibration elements does a 592XP have?
faq.a: There are several mounts in the system. Check the parts diagram for your saw to see each location and part.

faq.q: Can I keep running a saw with a broken AV mount?
faq.a: It is not a good idea. Control and comfort both suffer, and the remaining mounts take extra load.

name: Husqvarna Air Filter Cover for T540i XP
keyword: husqvarna t540i xp air filter cover
title: Husqvarna T540i XP Air Filter Cover
h1: Husqvarna T540i XP Air Filter Cover
meta: Husqvarna T540i XP air filter cover for the battery top-handle saw. Keeps dust and chips away from the motor and electronics. Fitting and cleaning tips here.
tagline: Replacement air filter cover for the Husqvarna T540i XP battery top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540i XP air filter cover fits the battery top-handle saw. Even battery saws pull cooling air through the housing, and a cracked or missing cover lets sawdust into places it should not go.
highlights: Air filter cover for the Husqvarna T540i XP
Keeps chips away from the motor cooling path
Fix for covers cracked or lost in the tree
Simple replacement with hand tools
Clean the filter area while the cover is off

body.h: Why a battery saw has an air filter cover
p: The T540i XP has no carburetor, but its motor and electronics still need cooling air. The air filter and cover keep sawdust out of that airflow. A climbing saw hangs in the dust all day, and fine chips packed into the housing can lead to heat problems.
Covers get cracked when saws are dropped or knocked against stems, and the clips can break with time.

Battery top-handle saws are often run all day by climbers on pruning and removal work, which means steady dust exposure. A blower or soft brush cleans the filter area quickly at lunch and at the end of the day. Do not wash the saw with water or a pressure washer. If the cover clips are getting loose or the cover rattles, replace it before it drops out of the tree.

Remove the battery first. Take off the old cover, clean out any dust and chips from the filter area and around the cooling path, and fit the new cover so it clips or screws down fully. Clean the area regularly, especially after cutting dry or dusty wood.
For the cooling fan, front handle and other T540i XP parts, see our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Does the T540i XP really need an air filter?
faq.a: Yes. It filters the cooling air for the motor and electronics, which helps the saw run without overheating.

faq.q: Will this cover fit the gas T540XP?
faq.a: No. The battery and gas saws use different housings. Order the part for your model.

name: Husqvarna Anti-Vibration Element Assembly for 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Anti-Vibration Element
meta: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II anti-vibration element assembly. Restores a firm handle feel and less buzz on this 50cc saw. Signs of wear and fitting notes here.
tagline: Anti-vibration element assembly for the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP Mark II anti-vibration element assembly replaces a worn or broken AV mount on the 50cc saw. When an element goes, the handles feel loose and more vibration reaches your hands.
highlights: Anti-vibration element assembly for the 550XP Mark II
Restores a firm, controlled handle feel
Cuts vibration reaching your hands
Replace when elements are broken, loose or stretched
Check the other AV mounts at the same time

p: The 550XP Mark II is a common crew saw for limbing and bucking, and it spends a lot of hours running. Anti-vibration elements fatigue, and a broken one changes how the saw feels. You might notice the rear handle sagging, the saw twisting in your grip or a new rattle.
Worn AV mounts make you work harder to control the saw and raise vibration exposure, which over time is hard on hands and arms.

A simple check is to hold the saw by the rear handle and front handle with the engine off and gently twist. A little give is normal, since the system is designed to flex. A clunk, a sagging handle or a lot of free play points to a broken element. Checking AV mounts during regular service helps keep a crew saw comfortable and in control on long days.

Check the parts diagram to see which location this assembly goes in. Remove the covers or handle needed for access, take out the old element and install the new one so it seats fully. Tighten fasteners to spec.
Inspect every AV element while the saw is apart and replace any that look tired. More 550XP Mark II parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Will this fit the original 550XP?
faq.a: Check the parts listing for your model. The Mark II has its own parts list.

faq.q: How do I know an AV element is broken?
faq.a: A loose or sagging handle, extra vibration and visible cracks or a separated spring or rubber are common signs.

name: Husqvarna Anti-Vibration Element for 572XP
title: Husqvarna 572XP Anti-Vibration Element
meta: Husqvarna 572XP anti-vibration element for worn or broken AV mounts. Restores control and cuts hand fatigue on this 70cc pro saw. Signs and fitting tips.
tagline: Replacement anti-vibration element for the Husqvarna 572XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP anti-vibration element replaces a worn or broken AV mount on the 70cc pro saw. Good AV mounts keep the handles solid and take the edge off engine vibration over a long day of felling and bucking.
highlights: Anti-vibration element for the Husqvarna 572XP
Restores a solid handle feel
Reduces vibration and hand fatigue
Common fix after a hard drop or heavy use
Pairs well with a front handle replacement

body.h: Why it matters on a pro saw
p: The 572XP is built for full days in the woods. That is a lot of vibration cycles through the AV system. When an element breaks, the saw can feel loose, the handles shift relative to the engine and more buzz reaches your hands.
A loose saw is harder to hold steady through a back cut or bore cut. Fresh AV mounts help you place the bar where you mean to.

Hand-arm vibration adds up over years of cutting. Good AV mounts, sharp chain and a well-tuned saw all reduce how much buzz reaches your hands. Anti-vibration gloves can help too. If you notice numbness, tingling or white fingers after running a saw, take it seriously, and look at the condition of the AV system on the saws you run most.
Check the parts diagram for the location, as the 572XP uses mounts in more than one spot. Remove the covers or handle needed for access, swap the element and tighten the fasteners to spec.
If you are replacing a bent front handle, it is a good time to inspect every AV mount. Find the front handle assembly and more in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Should I replace all the AV elements at once?
faq.a: If one has failed from age, the others have the same hours. Replacing a full set restores the saw's original feel.

faq.q: Can a broken AV element damage the saw?
faq.a: It puts extra load on the remaining mounts and can let parts rub. Replace it soon.

name: Husqvarna Bar Cover Nut
title: Husqvarna Bar Nut for Chainsaw Clutch Covers
h1: Husqvarna Bar Nut for Chainsaw Clutch Covers
meta: Replacement Husqvarna bar nut for the clutch cover. A lost or stripped nut stops a saw cold. Carry spares and confirm the thread for your model first.
tagline: Replacement nut that holds the bar and clutch cover on Husqvarna chainsaws.
summary: This Husqvarna bar nut holds the clutch cover and guide bar tight against the saw body. Nuts get lost in the grass during chain changes or stripped from overtightening, and without one the saw cannot run.
highlights: Replacement bar cover nut for Husqvarna saws
Holds the bar and clutch cover firmly in place
Cheap spare that can save a job
Fix for lost, rounded or stripped nuts
Confirm thread size for your model
specs: Check the parts listing for your model

p: Bar nuts come off every time you change a chain or flip a bar. Drop one in leaf litter or snow and the saw is done for the day. A couple of spares in the saw box or a pocket of the gear bag cost very little.
Overtightening with a long wrench can round the nut or damage the stud threads. Snug the nut firmly with the scrench after setting chain tension, without leaning on it.

If the clutch cover keeps loosening during cuts, check the nut, the stud and the cover itself. A cracked cover or a damaged stud can let the bar shift, and a loose bar throws chains and wears the rails. A good nut and a solid stud keep the bar clamped. Check tension again after the first few cuts with a new chain, since new chains stretch.

Husqvarna saws do not all use the same bar nut, so check the thread and style for your model. Some covers use captive nuts that stay in the cover. If the bar stud itself is damaged, replace it too, since a new nut will not hold on stripped threads.
Browse our chainsaw parts section for bar studs, clutch covers and other service items.

faq.q: Are all Husqvarna bar nuts the same?
faq.a: No. Thread size and style vary by model. Check the parts listing for your saw.

faq.q: How tight should the bar nut be?
faq.a: Firm with the standard scrench after setting chain tension. Follow the operator manual and do not use extension bars.

name: Husqvarna Bearings for T540XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna T540XP Mark II Bearings
meta: Husqvarna T540XP Mark II bearing replacement for this 37.7cc top-handle climbing saw. Signs of worn bearings, when to rebuild and why a pro shop helps here.
tagline: Replacement bearings for the Husqvarna T540XP Mark II top-handle saw.
summary: These Husqvarna T540XP Mark II bearings are replacement parts for engine rebuilds on the gas top-handle saw. Worn bearings show up as noise, play in the crankshaft and eventually seal failure, and are usually replaced during a major overhaul.
highlights: Replacement bearings for the T540XP Mark II
For engine overhaul and rebuild work
Fix for crankshaft play and bearing noise
Replace seals at the same time
Best done by an experienced saw tech

p: With the plug out and the clutch side exposed, a healthy crankshaft spins smoothly with no up-and-down or side-to-side play. Grinding, rumbling or noticeable play points to tired bearings. Worn bearings also let the crank move enough to wear out the seals, which causes air leaks and lean running.
A top-handle saw that has run for years in the canopy may reach that point. Check the parts diagram to confirm which bearing positions this part covers.

Worn bearings usually go along with other high-hour wear, so look at the piston, cylinder, clutch and AV mounts before deciding on a rebuild. On a top-handle saw that a climber relies on every day, many owners choose a full overhaul at once rather than repairing parts one at a time. Keep the saw's model and serial number on hand to order the correct bearings.

Bearing replacement means splitting the crankcase, pressing bearings out and in, and fitting new seals and gaskets. It takes the right tools and experience, and most climbers have a dealer or a saw tech do it.
Weigh the cost of a full rebuild against the saw's overall condition. Seals, gaskets and other T540XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Can I replace bearings without splitting the case?
faq.a: Main crankshaft bearings generally require splitting the case. Check the service manual for your saw.

faq.q: Should I replace seals with the bearings?
faq.a: Yes. New seals are standard practice whenever bearings are replaced.

name: Husqvarna Bushing for Chain Brake Hand Guard
title: Husqvarna Chain Brake Bushing for the Hand Guard
h1: Husqvarna Chain Brake Bushing for the Hand Guard
meta: Husqvarna chain brake bushing for the hand guard pivot. Restores smooth, reliable brake action. Signs of a worn bushing and why the chain brake must work.
tagline: Pivot bushing for the chain brake hand guard on Husqvarna chainsaws.
summary: This Husqvarna chain brake bushing sits at the pivot of the chain brake hand guard. A worn or missing bushing lets the guard flop or bind, which can affect how the chain brake engages.
highlights: Pivot bushing for the chain brake hand guard
Restores smooth, positive hand guard movement
Helps the chain brake engage as designed
Small part with a big safety role
Confirm fitment for your saw model
specs: Check the parts listing for your model

p: The chain brake is one of the main protections against kickback. The hand guard has to pivot freely so it can trip the brake, either from your hand pushing it forward or from inertia in a kickback. A worn bushing lets the guard wobble, and a damaged one can make it stick.
If the chain brake does not engage crisply and stop the chain, do not use the saw until it is fixed.

Sawdust, pitch and bar oil collect around the hand guard pivot. Clean the area during regular service and check the guard for side play. A guard that wobbles, sticks, or does not spring back fully may have a worn bushing, a weak spring or a damaged guard. If you are not sure the brake works correctly after the repair, have a dealer check it before the saw is used.

Check the parts diagram for your saw to confirm this is the right bushing. Remove the hand guard, take out the old bushing, fit the new one and reassemble with the correct fasteners. Then test the brake: it should snap on firmly and release cleanly.
If the guard itself is cracked or bent, replace it too. Find hand guards and other parts in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How do I test the chain brake?
faq.a: Follow the operator manual. The usual check is to engage the brake with the saw running at the right speed on a stable surface and confirm the chain stops immediately.

faq.q: Which saws use this bushing?
faq.a: It depends on the model. Check the parts listing or a Husqvarna parts lookup for your saw.

name: Husqvarna Chain Brake Hand Guard for T540i XP
keyword: husqvarna t540i xp chain brake hand guard
title: Husqvarna T540i XP Chain Brake Hand Guard
h1: Husqvarna T540i XP Chain Brake Hand Guard
meta: Husqvarna T540i XP chain brake hand guard for the battery top-handle saw. Replace cracked or bent guards so the brake works as designed. Fitting tips here.
tagline: Replacement chain brake hand guard for the Husqvarna T540i XP.
summary: This Husqvarna T540i XP chain brake hand guard is the front guard that also works the chain brake on the battery top-handle saw. A cracked or bent guard can keep the brake from engaging properly, so replace it before the saw goes back in the tree.
highlights: Chain brake hand guard for the T540i XP
Restores proper chain brake operation
Fix for guards cracked by drops or impacts
Protects your front hand
Test the brake after fitting

p: On a top-handle saw, the hand guard shields your front hand and trips the chain brake. Climbers rely on it when the saw kicks back in tight quarters. Guards get cracked when saws are dropped or swing into a stem on the lanyard, and a damaged guard may not trip the brake reliably.
Top-handle saws are made for trained arborists working aloft. Use them two-handed per ANSI Z133 and keep every safety feature working.

Check the hand guard every time you clean the saw. Look for cracks around the pivot, chips along the edge and play in the mounting. A guard that wobbles, rubs on the housing or does not travel fully forward needs attention. Climbers also tend to grab the guard when moving the saw around in the tree, so wear there shows up sooner than on a ground saw.
Remove the battery first. Remove the old guard per the service manual and fit the new one with the correct pivot hardware. If the pivot bushing is worn, replace it as well.
Test the brake before use: it should engage firmly and stop the chain, and release cleanly. For the front handle and other T540i XP parts, see our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Can I use the saw with a cracked hand guard?
faq.a: No. A damaged guard may not engage the chain brake. Replace it before using the saw.

faq.q: Is this the same guard as the gas T540XP?
faq.a: Do not assume so. Order the part listed for the T540i XP.

name: Husqvarna Chain Catcher
title: Husqvarna Chain Catcher Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna chain catcher. Helps stop a broken or derailed chain from whipping back at your hands. Why it matters and how to fit the right one.
tagline: Replacement chain catcher for Husqvarna chainsaws.
summary: This Husqvarna chain catcher is the small hook or bracket under the bar that grabs the chain if it breaks or jumps off. Chain catchers get chewed up by thrown chains and should be replaced when worn or broken.
highlights: Replacement chain catcher for Husqvarna saws
Helps catch a broken or thrown chain
Replace when chewed, bent or missing
Inexpensive safety part
Confirm fitment by saw model
specs: Check the parts listing for your model

p: When a chain breaks or comes off the bar, it can whip back toward the operator's right hand. The chain catcher sits just below the bar on the clutch side and is shaped to snag the chain before it gets that far. It is one of the standard safety features on a modern chainsaw.
Each time it catches a chain, it gets gouged. After a few hits it may be worn down to nothing.

The chain catcher is easy to overlook because it sits out of sight under the bar. Make it part of your routine check along with the chain brake, throttle lockout and muffler. A missing catcher often goes unnoticed until the next thrown chain, and that is the wrong time to find out. Keep a spare in the saw box along with a bar nut and a fuel filter.

Look at the catcher whenever you change a chain. If it is cracked, bent, worn through or missing, replace it. Most are held by a single screw or are part of a small bracket. Check your saw's parts listing, since catchers differ between models.
Keep chain tension right and chains sharp to reduce thrown chains in the first place. More parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Can I run my saw without a chain catcher?
faq.a: You should not. It is a safety feature meant to protect your hand if the chain breaks or derails.

faq.q: Why does my chain keep coming off?
faq.a: Loose tension, a worn bar, a worn sprocket or a dull chain are common causes. Check them before going back to work.

name: Husqvarna Chainsaw Starter Cord
title: Husqvarna Chainsaw Starter Rope Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna chainsaw starter rope. Fix a frayed or snapped pull cord before it strands you. Tips on cord length, fitting and keeping it from wearing.
tagline: Replacement starter cord for Husqvarna chainsaw recoil starters.
summary: This Husqvarna chainsaw starter rope replaces the pull cord in the recoil starter. A frayed cord tends to snap at the worst time, usually on a cold morning in the middle of a job, so it is worth swapping at the first sign of wear.
highlights: Replacement pull cord for Husqvarna recoil starters
Fix for frayed, glazed or snapped cords
Cheap spare for the saw box
Check cord diameter and length for your model
Inspect the starter pulley and spring while it is open
specs: Husqvarna chainsaw recoil starters; check size for your model

p: Every pull drags the cord across the starter housing eyelet. Over time it frays, glazes or wears thin. Pulling the cord at an angle, letting it snap back, or yanking it all the way to the end of its travel speeds that up.
Small and top-handle saws often use a thinner cord than larger saws, so confirm the right size for your model.

Carry a spare cord in the saw box. Restringing in the field is easier than walking back to the truck, and a snapped cord at the top of a removal can stop a whole crew. Cut the cord to the same length as the old one. A cord that is too long can tangle inside the starter, and one that is too short makes the saw harder to start.

Remove the starter housing, release spring tension carefully and remove the old cord. Thread the new cord, tie the knot as the old one was tied, and wind the pulley to preload the spring per the service manual. The handle should sit snug against the housing at rest. Wear eye protection when working with recoil springs.
Start the saw with a smooth pull, not a jerk. More service items are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: What size starter cord does my Husqvarna need?
faq.a: It depends on the model. Check the parts listing or operator manual for your saw.

faq.q: Why does my starter cord not retract?
faq.a: A broken or unhooked recoil spring, or a dirty or damaged pulley, are common causes. Inspect the starter assembly.

name: Husqvarna Choke Control Stop for 562XP
title: Husqvarna 562XP Choke Control Stop
meta: Husqvarna 562XP choke control stop replacement. Fixes a choke and stop control that will not hold position or shut the saw off cleanly. Fitting tips inside.
tagline: Choke and stop control part for the Husqvarna 562XP chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 562XP choke control stop is part of the combined choke and stop control on the 60cc saw. A broken or worn part can make the choke hard to set for starting, or stop the control from shutting the saw off properly.
highlights: Choke and stop control part for the Husqvarna 562XP
Restores proper choke operation for cold starts
Helps the stop function work as designed
Fix for broken or worn controls
Test start and stop before going back to work

p: On the 562XP, the choke and stop functions are combined in one control. Pulling it out sets the choke for a cold start, and moving it to the stop position shuts the engine down. A cracked or worn part in that linkage can leave the choke stuck, slipping or not seating, and can affect stopping.
A saw that will not shut off reliably needs to be repaired before it goes back to work.

Many 562XP starting complaints come from using the choke control wrong rather than from a broken part. Follow the starting procedure in the operator manual. If the control still feels loose, will not stay in position or will not move to stop, inspect the linkage. Plastic parts can crack from cold, impacts or force, and a new part restores a clean, positive feel.

Remove the top cover and air filter to get at the control. Check the parts diagram so you know where this part fits in the linkage, swap it and confirm the control moves through all positions smoothly.
Start the saw and check that the stop position shuts it down every time. Other 562XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: My 562XP will not shut off. Is it the choke control?
faq.a: It can be the control, the stop switch or the wiring. Stop using the saw and diagnose it before further use.

faq.q: Why will my choke not stay out?
faq.a: A worn or broken part in the choke control linkage is a common cause.

name: Husqvarna Clutch Assembly for 562XP
title: Husqvarna 562XP Clutch Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 562XP clutch assembly. Fixes slipping, chain creep at idle and broken clutch springs on this 60cc saw. Signs of wear and replacement tips inside.
tagline: Replacement centrifugal clutch for the Husqvarna 562XP chainsaw.
summary: This Husqvarna 562XP clutch assembly replaces the centrifugal clutch that drives the chain on the 60cc pro saw. A worn or broken clutch can slip under load, make the chain creep at idle or throw clutch pieces.
highlights: Centrifugal clutch assembly for the Husqvarna 562XP
Fixes slipping under load
Cures chain creep from broken or weak springs
Inspect the drum and sprocket at the same time
Use a piston stop and clutch tool for removal

p: The clutch engages as engine speed rises and lets go at idle. When the shoes wear or the springs fatigue, the chain may keep turning at idle, the saw may slip and smell hot in a deep cut, or you may hear rattling from the clutch side.
Chain movement at idle is a safety issue. If adjusting the idle does not stop it, the clutch needs attention.

Clutch problems often start with the chain. Running a dull chain makes you push harder and slip the clutch more, which heats and wears the shoes. Keeping chains sharp and the right tension takes a lot of load off the drivetrain. Also clean the clutch area regularly, since packed sawdust and oil around the drum hold heat and wear parts faster.

Remove the bar, chain and clutch cover, fit a piston stop through the plug hole and unscrew the clutch with the correct tool. Note that most Husqvarna clutches use a left-hand thread. Inspect the clutch drum, sprocket and needle bearing and replace any that are worn.
Fit the new clutch, torque it per the service manual and test the idle. Sprockets and other 562XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Which way does the 562XP clutch unscrew?
faq.a: Husqvarna clutches typically use a left-hand thread, so turn clockwise to loosen. Confirm in the service manual.

faq.q: Should I replace the sprocket with the clutch?
faq.a: If the sprocket or drum is worn, yes. A worn sprocket also wears out new chain faster.

name: Husqvarna Cooling Fan for T540i XP Battery Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna T540i XP Cooling Fan
meta: Husqvarna T540i XP cooling fan for the battery top-handle saw. Keeps the motor and electronics cool on long climbs. Signs of a damaged fan and fitting tips.
tagline: Replacement motor cooling fan for the Husqvarna T540i XP battery saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540i XP cooling fan is the cooling fan for the motor on the battery top-handle saw. A cracked or damaged fan reduces airflow, which can lead to the saw overheating or cutting out during heavy use.
highlights: Cooling fan for the Husqvarna T540i XP
Keeps the motor and electronics cool
Fix for cracked, chipped or noisy fans
Clear dust from the cooling path at the same time
Remove the battery before service

p: Battery saws make heat under load, and the T540i XP is designed to work hard in the canopy. The fan moves air across the motor and electronics. If blades are broken or the fan is damaged, airflow drops, and you may see the saw slow down or stop to protect itself on long cuts.
A rattle or new noise from the motor area can also point to a damaged fan.

Batteries and saws run warmer on hot days and in dense, hard wood. Keep a second battery in the shade and swap them as needed rather than pushing one battery to its limit. Fine sawdust from dry wood collects quickly around the fan, so check it often. If the saw still overheats with a clean, intact fan and filter, have a dealer look at it.

Remove the battery first. Follow the service manual to reach the fan, remove the old one, clean out dust and chips, and fit the new fan securely. Spin it by hand to confirm it turns freely without rubbing.
Keep the air filter and cover clean and the cooling vents clear. Matching T540i XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Why does my T540i XP shut off when it gets hot?
faq.a: Battery saws protect themselves from overheating. Check that the cooling path, filter and fan are clean and intact, and let the saw and battery cool.

faq.q: Is this a job I can do myself?
faq.a: If you are comfortable with basic service and follow the manual, yes. Otherwise a Husqvarna dealer can do it.

name: Husqvarna Cylinder and Piston Kit for 372XP
title: Husqvarna 372XP Cylinder and Piston Kit
meta: Husqvarna 372XP cylinder and piston kit for top-end rebuilds on the 70.7cc saw. When a rebuild makes sense, what to check and how to protect the new parts.
tagline: OEM cylinder and piston kit for rebuilding the top end of a Husqvarna 372XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP cylinder and piston kit pairs a cylinder and piston for a full top-end rebuild on the 70.7cc saw. It is the fix for a scored piston, worn cylinder or low compression on a saw that is otherwise worth keeping.
highlights: Cylinder and piston kit for the Husqvarna 372XP
Restores compression and power
Fix for scored or worn top ends
Find and fix the cause of the failure first
Use new gaskets and test for air leaks

p: Pistons rarely fail on their own. The usual causes are a lean condition from an air leak, a clogged fuel filter or a bad carburetor setting; bad fuel mix; or dirt getting past the air filter. If you drop a new kit on without finding the cause, it can fail the same way.
Check the intake boot, crank seals, fuel line and filter, and air filter before and during the rebuild.

Measure compression before and after the job with a proper gauge so you have a baseline for later. Note it in your shop log along with the date and hours. Many crews keep a 372XP running for years with one or two top-end jobs, and a clear record makes it easier to see when it is time for the next one, or when the saw has reached the end of its life.

Fit the piston with the arrow facing the exhaust side as marked, use new circlips and a new base gasket, and torque the cylinder evenly to the service manual spec. A pressure and vacuum test before startup is strongly recommended.
Run the first tanks with a properly mixed fuel and avoid long full-throttle cuts at first. Gaskets and seals are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Is a rebuild worth it on a 372XP?
faq.a: Often, yes. The 372XP is a durable saw, and a top end rebuild can give it years more work if the bottom end is healthy.

faq.q: What causes a 372XP piston to score?
faq.a: Lean running from air leaks or fuel starvation, wrong fuel mix, or dirt in the intake are the common causes.

name: Husqvarna Cylinder Assembly for 572XP
title: Husqvarna 572XP Cylinder Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 572XP cylinder assembly for top-end rebuilds on the 70.6cc pro saw. When a new cylinder makes sense, what to replace with it and how to avoid repeats.
tagline: OEM cylinder assembly for rebuilding the top end of a Husqvarna 572XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 572XP cylinder assembly replaces the cylinder on the 70.6cc pro saw. It is the core part of a top-end rebuild when the cylinder is scored, worn or damaged.
highlights: Cylinder assembly for the Husqvarna 572XP
Restores compression and cutting power
Fix for scored or worn cylinders
Use with a new base gasket
Check the piston and find the root cause

p: Light scuffing can sometimes be cleaned up, but deep scoring, a worn coating or damage to the bore means a new cylinder. Low compression, hard starting and lost power on a 572XP that is otherwise healthy are typical reasons to look at the top end.
Confirm what the listing includes. If the piston is worn or scored, replace it at the same time.

A new cylinder is a big investment, so take care with break-in. Use fresh fuel mixed at the ratio in the operator manual, warm the saw up before heavy cuts, and check that the carburetor is not set too lean. Recheck the saw after the first few tanks. A pressure and vacuum test is also cheap insurance before the saw goes back to full-time work.

Find the cause of the failure first: check the intake, crank seals, fuel system and air filter. Use a new base gasket, install the piston correctly, and torque the cylinder fasteners evenly to spec. A pressure and vacuum test before startup is the best check.
If you are not set up for engine work, a dealer can do the job. The matching gasket is in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Does the cylinder assembly include a piston?
faq.a: Check the listing. Some cylinder assemblies come with a piston, and some do not.

faq.q: Do I need a new gasket?
faq.a: Yes. Always fit a new cylinder base gasket when the cylinder comes off.

name: Husqvarna Cylinder Cover Assembly for T540XP
title: Husqvarna T540XP Cylinder Cover Assembly
meta: Husqvarna T540XP cylinder cover assembly for the gas top-handle climbing saw. Replaces cracked or lost covers that let chips at the air filter. Fitting tips.
tagline: Replacement top cover assembly for the Husqvarna T540XP top-handle saw.
summary: This Husqvarna T540XP cylinder cover assembly replaces the top cover on the gas top-handle saw. On a climbing saw that gets bumped and dropped, the cover can crack or lose its latch, letting chips toward the air filter.
highlights: Cylinder cover assembly for the Husqvarna T540XP
Shields the air filter, plug and cylinder
Fix for cracked covers and broken latches
Quick swap with hand tools
Confirm original T540XP or Mark II before ordering

p: The cylinder cover keeps sawdust and moisture away from the air filter and spark plug and helps direct cooling air. Climbers drop saws onto lanyards and knock them against stems, and covers take the hit. A cracked cover lets fine dust work toward the intake, which wears the engine.
A loose cover can also rattle off and fall out of the tree, which is a hazard for the ground crew.

When cleaning the air filter on a top-handle saw, do it on the ground, not in the tree, so the cover and filter cannot fall. Keep the old cover's fasteners as spares if they are in good shape. If your saw's cover has a quick-release latch, make sure it locks firmly in place before you send the saw back up on the tool line.
Remove the old cover, clean around the air filter and cylinder fins, and fit the new cover so it seats evenly with the latch or fasteners fully engaged. Check the air filter and plug while it is off.
The T540XP and T540XP Mark II have different part lists, so confirm your model. More T540XP parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: Will this fit the T540XP Mark II?
faq.a: Check the parts listing for your exact model. Mark II parts are not always interchangeable.

faq.q: How often should I clean under the cylinder cover?
faq.a: Check it daily on a saw in regular use, and clean the air filter and fins whenever chips build up.
